roleContext.jobDescription: A soft-drinks manufacturer forecasts weekly demand for around 900 products across grocery, convenience and wholesale channels. The data scientist builds features for and validates the forecasting models in Python, maintains the feature pipelines, presents forecast accuracy to supply planning and documents models to the company's standard. The team wants someone who has owned a forecasting model across its lifecycle, deciding which model changes go ahead and leading the business sign-off with the planning managers. The analytics team of five reports to the head of supply planning and works from the company's Airflow and data-warehouse stack.

candidate.originalCvMarkdown:
# Curriculum vitae

Target role: Data Scientist, Demand Forecasting

## Experience

- Data analyst, then data scientist, at Brightwater Beverages from January 2020 to April 2024, in a demand-planning analytics team of five.
- Built the promotional-uplift features (discount depth, display flags, competitor promotions) for the weekly SKU-level forecasting model and kept them running as a scheduled Airflow pipeline.
- Ran the monthly backtests of the gradient-boosted forecasting model and wrote up the results for the lead data scientist, who decided which model changes went forward.
- Presented the monthly forecast-accuracy review to the supply-planning team, with bias and error broken down by product category and channel, and the actions agreed with the planners.
- Wrote the input-data and known-limitations sections of the forecasting model's model card, following the team's documentation template.

## Work samples

- Work sample: a slide deck the candidate titled 'My year on the forecasting model'. Its closing slide, 'What people said', quotes the planning manager ('owned that model from first prototype to sign-off') and a teammate ('the brains behind every model decision'); the earlier slides list the model's input features.
